notes: Documents are written the way real postmortems, ADRs, ownership pages and Slack threads read, not tuned to the extractor. A case passes only if every must_surface source reaches the briefing, no must_not_surface source does, and the approval call matches.

documents.title: Postmortem: duplicate card charges (Nov 2025)
documents.content: On Nov 14, 2,300 customers were charged twice for a single checkout. The retry wrapper in payments-service re-sent card authorization requests after a processor timeout without an idempotency key. The processor had already accepted the first request, so both went through. Every retry of a card authorization must carry the original idempotency key.

documents.title: ADR-014: Ledger writes go through ledger-service
documents.content: Status: accepted, March 2025. We decided that no service writes to the ledger database directly. All balance changes must use the ledger-service API so that every adjustment is journaled.

documents.title: ADR-009: Payment sessions in Redis
documents.content: Status: accepted, January 2024. We decided payments-service should store checkout sessions in Redis for low-latency reads.

documents.title: ADR-021: Move payment sessions to PostgreSQL
documents.content: Status: accepted, June 2025. Supersedes ADR-009. After Redis evictions dropped live checkout sessions, we decided payments-service must use PostgreSQL for checkout sessions instead of Redis.

documents.title: Service ownership
documents.content: payments-service is owned by the Payments Core team. ledger-service is owned by the Ledger team. notification-worker is owned by the Growth team. fraud-engine is owned by the Risk team, and changes to it need a Risk reviewer.

documents.title: Architecture overview
documents.content: checkout-gateway depends on payments-service for card authorization. payments-service depends on ledger-service and fraud-engine. billing-service depends on ledger-service for invoice balances. All services share the primary PostgreSQL cluster pg-main.

documents.title: Change management policy
documents.content: Changes to payments-service or ledger-service during the holiday freeze (Nov 20 to Jan 5) are prohibited without VP Engineering approval. Database migrations on pg-main must be reviewed by the Ledger team.

documents.title: Incident: notification-worker retry storm (Aug 2025)
documents.content: A bug in the notification-worker retry loop sent 40,000 duplicate marketing emails after an SMTP timeout. The Growth team capped retries at three.

documents.title: #payments-eng thread
documents.content: Heads up: fraud-engine timeouts spike whenever payments-service raises its worker concurrency above 64, because each worker opens its own fraud-engine connection.

documents.title: Outage: ledger-service connection pool exhaustion (Feb 2026)
documents.content: ledger-service failed for 47 minutes after the billing-service month-end backfill opened 400 connections to pg-main. Backfills must run through the throttled batch queue.

documents.title: Runbook: rotate the payments processor API key
documents.content: Run `make rotate-processor-key ENV=prod` from the payments-service repo, then restart pods one at a time while watching authorization error rates.
